rounds.text: Ameya Precision Engineers Ltd trades at compelling valuation discounts relative to its sector, offering a P/E of 12.48x against a sector benchmark of 22.41x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.31x compared to the sector's 12.72x [E6, E11]. Profit growth is accelerating aggressively, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 36% and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 44% [E18, E19]. Operating margins are expanding robustly, reaching 19% in March 2026—a 9 percentage point increase over three years—while return on capital employed sits at an impressive 25.31%, well above the sector median of 13.3% [E10, E25, E69]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 243 per share, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 30.1% [E39, E40], supported by a high rules-based screen score of 90 out of 100 [E57] and strong macroeconomic tailwinds in the Capital Goods sector [E64, E66]. Conceded: cash conversion is weak at 0.35x against reported profit, with debtor days increasing to 115 days [E29, E56].

Ameya Precision Engineers Ltd trades at the absolute peak of its 52-week range [E5, E42, E43], accompanied by a high annualised volatility of 53.0% [E48] and a history of deep drawdowns reaching -48.9% [E47]. This price momentum has outpaced underlying fundamental reality, with recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 32% [E51] and earnings growth visibly decelerating [E62]. Underlying top-line expansion remains lackluster, reflected in a poor compounded sales growth of 10% over five years [E14, E55] that has further slowed to just 4% over the trailing twelve months [E16]. Operational efficiency is also undermined by deteriorating working capital management, as debtor days have stretched from 91.8 to 115 days [E56]. This disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation is starkly highlighted by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.35x [E29] and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.06 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31]. Furthermore, despite reporting profits, the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E54] and has newly incurred borrowings up to Rs 0.18 Cr [E34].
